page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.12xlarge is an ARM-based general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors on the ARMv9 architecture. The system provides 48 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core running at 2.8 GHz. It features 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core, alongside 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARM AES instructions. With 192 GB of total memory, the instance maintains a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core, complemented by 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong multithreaded and memory-subsystem performance alongside exceptional local I/O handling. In multicore evaluations, the instance reached the top 10% bracket in Geekbench multicore (23,688) and software compilation using Clang (71,286), while stress-ng multi-core testing placed in the top 25% (81,856.85). Memory throughput is a key strength, recording over 400 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth and 208.86 GB/sec write bandwidth, securing top-tier positions in PassMark memory and database operations tests. Furthermore, web serving throughput exceeded 103 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value processing demonstrated 100.66 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff lies between single-threaded velocity and aggregate core scaling. While multi-core throughput and compilation tasks place in top-tier tiers, single-core benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,847.0) and stress-ng single-core occupy the middle 50% band. From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture delivers high core density and memory bandwidth at favorable operational efficiency compared to traditional x86 alternatives, especially when taking advantage of the included 2850 GB NVMe storage volume without external volume overhead.

The Amazon Web Services m8gd.12xlarge is well structured for large-scale multithreaded workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and low-latency ephemeral disk storage. It is directly suited for medium-to-large relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching systems, large distributed build and CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservice fleets, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.12xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz, 192 GB of memory, and 2850 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside 22 Gbps baseline networking. Memory bandwidth and multicore efficiency are notable strengths, achieving top-tier ratings in PassMark database operations, Clang code compilation, large-block memory read/write operations, and static web serving throughput. Single-core compute scores remain in the middle percentile tier, reflecting an architectural emphasis on multithreaded density rather than raw single-thread clock frequency. The combination of dedicated physical cores, balanced memory density, and bundled fast local storage makes this instance effective for heavy relational databases, caching tiers, continuous integration build servers, and container cluster hosts.
